articles.title_orig: Stocks slide again as Treasury yields push higher, Oracle leads Nasdaq lower: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stocks slide again as Treasury yields push higher, Oracle leads Nasdaq lower: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
The jump in Treasury yields this week is delivering a reality check about a strong economy, stubborn inflation, and the growing cost of the national debt .
That will put the squeeze on the debt-heavy Trump administration as it tries to find a path forward for the economy.
It also highlights the tension between the nation's top two economic policymakers. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh wants to hear what markets are saying. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants to use his tools to change the message when he believes it's wrong.
Bond yields jumped Wednesday, and were trading near multiple-decade highs Thursday , as traders digested surprisingly positive purchasing managers indices against the backdrop of a Fed that as of last week has started hiking its short-term policy rate. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 10 basis points to 4.87%, while the 10-year Treasury rose 17 basis points to 5.12% Thursday morning.
Those yields are extraordinary by recent standards but less so over a longer horizon. The 10-year Treasury averaged about 5.9% from 1990 through 2006, before years of slow growth and usually low interest rates reset Americans' expectations about borrowing costs.
Now the economy looks stronger, propelled in part by a surge in investment in artificial intelligence . Competition for capital has contributed to higher interest rates.
The boom appears to go deeper. The Census Bureau reported last week that real median household income rose 2.6% to $87,460 and the poverty rate fell by half a percentage point to 10.2%.
The economy's recent strength has also come on the back of a flood of government deficit spending, driven in part by large tax cuts under the first and second Trump administrations, with Iran war spending piling on. The federal deficit is set to come in above 6% of gross domestic product this year, based on data from the Congressional Budget Office. The agency projects that the tax-and-policy law passed last year will raise deficits by $4.7 trillion over 10 years, though tariffs will offset some of that.
The nation is awash in credit. Warsh pointed to heavy debt issuance by banks and other financial institutions and tight credit spreads — suggesting borrowers have little trouble seeking loans — as among the key factors that prompted him to vote with the rest of the Fed's policymakers to raise interest rates.
In the days since, several other Fed officials, including Governor Michael Barr on Wednesday, said they thought more rate increases would likely be needed.
Bond yields likely benefitted from Warsh's decision to raise interest rates this week. Had Warsh not acted on inflation, traders would have run up long-term yields to account for the uncertainty of when and how the Fed might act.
But Warsh will only go so far to influence the 10-year. "Ensuring continuous, sustainable, durable, economic growth, that's the business we're in," he said last week. Warsh and the Fed will act to try to tamp down the risk of inflation, but he doesn't want to induce a recession.
The Fed's decision to move up interest rates highlights the possibility for tension with the Treasury Department.
Warsh treats the 10-year Treasury as a vital source of information about the economy. He called it "the most important asset anywhere in the world" at his most recent press conference. He has changed the way the Fed communicates to make it easier for him to read the market's unfiltered signal.
Bessent , on the other hand, has shown willingness to intervene when he believes markets have moved away from equilibrium. He recently ramped up the Treasury's efforts to buy back some long-term debt maturities because he saw a "fever" in the markets.
"I don't believe that I can change the equilibrium price, but nothing's ever in equilibrium," Bessent said at a Breitbart event on Sept. 8. "When there's a disequilibrium, my job is to try to push things back towards equilibrium," he said.
The stakes are growing because the Treasury must refinance a huge stock of debt while continuing to refinance large deficits. Some in the markets expect the Treasury to cut the supply of long-term debt it issues in favor of more short-term bills.
That can get expensive for the U.S. government, and the taxpayer, when the Fed is raising short-term interest rates.
Higher long-term rates compound the risks. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget calculates that the 10-year Treasury at 5% is about 80 basis points above CBO's baseline. If it stays that way over the coming decade, interest costs would rise to an annual $2.7 trillion — more than Social Security or Medicare, the nonpartisan group said.
Higher average interest rates also mean U.S. growth has to stay higher for longer for the nation to have any chance at growing its way out of debt.
That already looks unlikely. The International Monetary Fund estimated earlier this year that the U.S. government would need to run a primary budget surplus of 1% of GDP to put U.S. debt on a downward trajectory.
With President Donald Trump promising $5,000 checks if Republicans sweep the midterm election , a turn toward fiscal rectitude looks unlikely.
The bond market doesn't care about the politics. It's rendering a verdict about the cost of capital in a strong economy with continuing inflation pressure and vast government borrowing needs.
Policymakers may not like that judgment, but they can't ignore it.

articles.title_orig: FDA nominee contradicts Trump on safety of measles vaccine
articles.title_zh: FDA nominee contradicts Trump on safety of measles vaccine
articles.content_orig:
Dr Heidi Overton faces confirmation hearing weeks after standing behind Trump as he suggested shot could be ‘quite lethal’
Dr Heidi Overton, Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), has told senators the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is “safe and effective”, weeks after standing behind the president as he suggested the shot could be “quite lethal” .
At a confirmation hearing on Thursday, Overton described the MMR vaccine as “safe and effective”, adding: “It is our best tool right now in the public health response to the measles outbreak.”
Asked whether any vaccine on the US market was unsafe, she said: “Every vaccine on the US market right now is safe and effective according to the FDA.”
Overton faced questions from Bill Cassidy, the Louisiana Republican and physician who chairs the Senate health committee, whose vote is seen as pivotal. He had called her role in Trump’s August vaccine executive order “almost disqualifying”.
The hearing comes as the US records its highest number of measles cases since 1991.
When Cassidy asked what Overton would do if the president asked her to break those assurances on vaccine safety, she replied: “I would give him my best advice, and I would follow the statutory requirements for the role of FDA commissioner regarding individual product determinations for safety and efficacy.”
When Bernie Sanders, the independent Vermont senator, asked whether she would have “the courage to stand up to” a president who he said “lies all of the time”, Overton did not answer directly. “I have worked for the president for a long time now, and earned his trust because I have been part of robust discussions to bring him the best advice,” she said.
In her opening statement, Overton framed her agenda around speeding up drug development to protect US leadership in biotechnology. “We can protect America’s global leadership in biotechnology, but we have to act fast,” she said, pledging to make the FDA “the agency of the possible, rather than the impossible”.
Overton, whose father leads a church in her home town of Gallup, New Mexico, has described Colossians 3:23 (“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters”) as one of her life verses since childhood.
Susan Collins, the Maine Republican senator, challenged her over the FDA’s August authorization of flavored vapes and nicotine pouches, including blueberry, mango and cappuccino. Collins said nearly 90% of young e-cigarette users choose flavored products.
Overton said there was “100% agreement from this administration that we must protect kids”, but defended the decision as recommended by career staff because “so many adults are using flavors preferentially”. She added: “If that standard is not appropriate, we should work on statutes to fix that.”
If confirmed, Overton, 37, would be the youngest ever FDA commissioner. A surgeon by training, she is now deputy assistant to the president for domestic policy, and served as a White House fellow during Trump’s first term.
In a February 2023 issue brief for the conservative America First Policy Institute, where she was chief policy officer, she criticized federal policies that allowed abortion pills to be sent through the mail, writing that abortion “is corrosive to children, women, and society broadly”.
She would replace Marty Makary, who resigned in May, and take over an agency still recovering from 2025 layoffs that cut its workforce by nearly 20%.

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia thwarts Houthi ballistic missiles, Yemen's Saudi-led coalition says
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia thwarts Houthi ballistic missiles, Yemen's Saudi-led coalition says
articles.content_orig:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have been firing on Saudi Arabia from Yemen.
President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28, with massive joint U.S.-Israeli strikes targeting military, government and infrastructure sites.
Delegations from the U.S. and Iran entered negotiations in June aimed at a war-ending deal based on a memorandum of understanding signed by both countries.
Those talks broke down as the U.S. and Iran continued to exchange strikes, with the strategic Strait of Hormuz as the primary flashpoint. Trump then said in August that the U.S. would launch a "crushing economic operation" to force Tehran into submission.
Saudi forces intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday, a military spokesperson said, following safety alerts issued for five regions of the country.
Col. Turki Al-Malki, the spokesperson for Saudi-led coalition forces operating in support of the internationally-backed Yemeni government, said in posts to X that air defenses "thwarted an attempt to target Taif and Yanbu," two of the five regions put under safety alert.
"Escalations and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly," he added.
The Saudi General Directorate of Civil Defence on Thursday issued safety alerts for five regions amid continued cross-border hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
The directorate posted safety alerts to X for the regions of Yanbu, Tabuk, Taif, Mecca and Jeddah.
All warnings were lifted soon after they were announced, with the directorate saying that the "danger has passed."
Senior Iranian figures praised Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's Wednesday address to the United Nations General Assembly, in which he said Tehran "will never bow" to U.S. threats.
Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi, the chief of staff of the Iranian armed forces, wrote in a post on X that Pezeshkian's speech constituted "a slap in the face" to the U.S., after President Donald Trump said he was mulling a "big decision" at to whether to make a deal with Tehran or "quickly annihilate" the country.
"As long as Iran's waters, land and skies remain under threat, no aggressor nation -- nor any supporter of such aggressors -- shall enjoy security," Abdollahi said.
The speaker of the Iranian parliament and Tehran's chief negotiator, Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, said in a post to X that Pezeshkian "spoke not just for a government, but for a 3,000-year-old civilization. He was the powerful voice of courage, resilience and strength for the Islamic Republic of Iran."
Iran has been forced to cancel regional international flights because of pressure from U.S. sanctions, Iranian officials said.
Iranian media, citing the Civil Aviation Authority, said Baghdad, Iraq, Oman and Azerbaijan will no longer receive flights from Iran. Four Iraq flights were being re-routed to Najaf, Iraq.
Austrian Airlines said in a statement to ABC News that it suspended operations to and from Tehran until Oct. 24. FlyDubai also said it is no longer operating flights to Iran.

articles.title_orig: Ethiopia's army says it has repelled TPLF attacks in first comment on fresh Tigray fighting
articles.title_zh: Ethiopia's army says it has repelled TPLF attacks in first comment on fresh Tigray fighting
articles.content_orig:
Tigrayan fighters have been seen on the streets of the region's main city but it is relatively quiet there as clashes flare up elsewhere
Ethiopia's army says it has repelled attacks from Tigrayan forces and their allies in parts of the north of the country, in its first statement since fighting broke out on Wednesday.
The army said hostilities began in an area of Amhara region close to the border with Tigray, adding that its soldiers had inflicted heavy casualties and seized weapons.
The developments come as tensions between the federal government and Tigrayan leaders have sharply escalated over the last few days, raising fears that a devastating civil war could resume.
On Wednesday, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which dominates the region, seized control of three airports from federal police.
The TPLF has not commented on the army's claims and the BBC has not been able to independently verify the army's claims.
The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and surrounding areas.
There are unconfirmed reports that TPLF forces have launched attacks in the neighbouring regions of Afar and Amhara.
A humanitarian source in Afar told AFP news agency on Thursday that Tigrayan forces had launched heavy artillery attacks as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the border with Tigray.
"We are in the situation of full-blown war now," TPLF vice-president Amanuel Assefa is quoted by the news agency as saying.
The latest escalation follows months of rising tensions between Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government and Tigray authorities, who fought a devastating war from 2020 to 2022.
That ended in an African Union-brokered peace deal but over recent months both sides have been accusing each other of violating the agreement.
It was one of the most deadly conflicts this century - the AU's mediator estimated some 600,000 people died as the fighting drove the region to the precipice of famine.
On Sunday, the TPLF announced an alliance with six other armed groups to oust the government.
Following the seizure of the airports, Ethiopian Airlines has cancelled all flights to Tigray.
Residents of Tigray's main city of Mekelle told the BBC that local forces had taken over control of the city's airport from the national police early on Wednesday.
This followed reports of drone strikes in Tigray in recent days.
A Mekelle resident told the BBC's Newsday programme on Thursday there had been no clashes in the city, unlike in the previous war, with most fighting happening elsewhere.
Tigray capital 'out of cash' as fighting escalates
"Mekelle is calm, except the stress from the people," said the resident, only identified as Fitsum for his safety. He added that the biggest problem was economic, with people not having enough cash.
"People are in a mood where they are distressed because it's been so difficult, so tough. The last seven or eight months the government has been denying budgets to the civil servants and all the banks were running out of cash."
Fitsum said people had been relying on mobile banking but with the risk of communications being cut off, "people are going to be in grave danger because there is almost no cash".
With the outbreak of war, people were limiting their movements and the city was all quiet - "it's like a curfew has been placed," he told the BBC.

articles.title_orig: Dolly Parton's sister defends iconic singer's nephew over restraining order: 'We all love Bryan.'
articles.title_zh: Dolly Parton's sister defends iconic singer's nephew over restraining order: 'We all love Bryan.'
articles.content_orig:
Dolly Parton died in August at the age of 80
Dolly Parton's management company has accused her nephew of "threats, intimidation, and coercion", revealing a bitter battle over the late star's legacy and business interests.
The accusations against Bryan Seaver, who was Parton's head of security and was handpicked to announce her death last month, have been made public in US legal documents filed this week.
The company that manages Parton's businesses and properties, She's Alive, is seeking a temporary civil restraining order against him.
In court filings, She's Alive alleged that Seaver mounted "an obscene, deliberate and escalating campaign of threats", claiming he said he would ruin her empire if the estate did not pay him. He has denied the claims.
In a statement to TMZ , external , he said that text messages and emails quoted in the court application had been taken out of context to make it look like he was threatening people.
"Nothing in this lawsuit were threats and most of the comments I stand by," he said.
"A lot of these messages are two guys having rage talk and crying on the phone together while we were grieving."
Seaver, the son of Parton's sister Cassie, owns a company that provided the singer's  security detail for the last 20 years of her life.
Last week, he was fired by She's Alive as head of security for her properties.
In a statement at the time, Seaver and his company said the dismissal was "unexpected" and "unexplained".
They added: "We refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much."
Bryan Seaver announced the news of his aunt's death to the world in August
The request for a restraining order was filed in Nashville on Tuesday by She's Alive, which is run by Parton's longtime manager Danny Nozell.
The court documents quoted a series of exchanges in which someone, identified by the estate as Seaver, threatened to destroy Parton's brand.
In one, he's alleged to have said he would become "the hand of retribution for my entire family", according to the court documents.
Another said: "I'm going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly's brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It's going to be great. Or [expletive] pay me."
The papers also claimed that Seaver used his experience as a military contractor to intimidate employees.
In an exchange with one of Parton's lawyers, he allegedly described himself as a "killer" and said that on the day his aunt died, he had sold $27m (Â£20m) in arms and ammunition to the Haitian police.
"All I do is warfare... Everyone needs to be worried about what I might do," he was accused of saying, according to a copy of an email attached to the complaint.
In his statement published on TMZ, Seaver said: "I am a career soldier and military contractor and do conduct arms deals for foreign governments. I am a security professional and I am a killer."
But he denied making threats and said he had been "talking frankly in a private way with Danny who I thought was my friend".
The messages have resulted in some employees and lawyers for Parton's trusts and estates resigning, according to the court documents.
She's Alive has also had to hire private security for its employees, including at their homes, the filing states.
The BBC has contacted Seaver and She's Alive for further comment.
Previously, Seaver was known to the public for announcing his aunt's death in a video posted to her Instagram account on 25 August.
Speaking in front of a black background, he was sombre and reflective as he introduced himself and shared the unexpected news.
"This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality," he said in the video.
Seaver added that he had followed in his father Larry's footsteps in becoming Parton's head of security, a post he held for more than 20 years.
Nozell started working for Parton in 2004, first as a tour consultant and later as her manager.
In the 2019 Netflix film, Dolly Parton: Here I Am, he said his job was to transform her from a "heritage act" into a "superstar", and he took responsibility for reviving her international touring career.
In a statement last month, he said the singer had "worked up until the day she died" on multiple projects, and envisioned a legacy that continued long beyond her death.
"She loved seeing her dreams come to life, and loved knowing her work brought people joy," he said in the statement.
"Ever the planner, Dolly worked with the team that she handpicked, for the past several years to build a project roadmap that will guide us for decades to come."
The estate now faces a public tug of war over that legacy.

articles.title_orig: Meta Debuts Dedicated ‘Charm’ Device for Using Muse AI
articles.title_zh: Meta Debuts Dedicated ‘Charm’ Device for Using Muse AI
articles.content_orig:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is continuing his metaverse while simultaneously pushing forward on AI agents.
At Meta Connect , the Facebook co-founder revealed on Wednesday the Meta VR Glasses, a smaller and slimmer device compared to the company's older Quest-branded family of VR headsets, and a handheld device called the Muse Charm that works with the company's recently released Muse AI personal agent . He revealed the products while speaking on stage at the annual Connect conference for developers.
Zuckerberg shared few details about what Muse Charm can do, only to say that people will be able to speak to the gadget to interact with their Meta AI agents "without having to unlock a phone or open an app." He didn't say how much it would cost, but said that Meta needs to "finalize laying out the components" and is "planning to have this ready to ship in time for the holidays in December."
"We've packed a lot of technology with this little guy," Zuckerberg said. "So, if you're not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show it what's going on around you."
The Meta VR Glasses are slimmer and lighter than the company's older Quest-branded VR headsets, but they are also more expensive, costing $1,299 when they go on sale in spring 2027. They represent Meta's first VR device since 2024, when the company debuted the $299 Quest 3S.
The Meta VR Glasses are powered by an external puck that houses a Qualcomm processor and battery, allowing it to function as a mini-computer that also helps reduce the glasses' overall weight and size. The glasses are able to display better visuals than the older Quest headset, and contain sensors that track users' eyes and hand movements, which reduces the need to use controllers to interact with the device.
"We have built a new kind of VR device that delivers the same magical feeling of presence and immersion, high-resolution displays and views of the world around you in a form factor that is a pair of glasses for the first time," Zuckerberg said.

articles.content_orig:
By LAURA FOX, ASSOCIATE SHOWBUSINESS EDITOR
Published: 10:50 EDT, 24 September 2026 | Updated: 12:07 EDT, 24 September 2026
Macklemore has announced a string of Free Palestine gigs, after being kicked off Ed Sheeran 's tour sparked a huge backlash.
The rapper was dropped as a support act from Ed's Loop tour over pro-Palestine comments he made at the singer's New Jersey shows earlier this month.
After Macklemore was dropped from performing at upcoming dates, all of Sheeran’s opening acts – Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe, as well as his backing band Beoga – announced they would be leaving the tour in solidarity with the rapper and Palestine .
Ed has since been accused of 'bowing to the mob' after he apologised to his fans for his handling of the row.
In a post on Instagram, Macklemore said that his 'schedule has freed up a bit' in the wake of being axed from the Loop tour.
The star then announced he would be performing concerts in Dublin, Paris and London, beginning on October 26, with proceeds 'benefitting organisations supporting the Palestinian people and movement'.
He wrote: 'If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it’s that something has shifted over the last three years.

'There has been a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now.
'It’s 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn’t work anymore. People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community.
'To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it.
'What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage. When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention.
'So, as you all know, my schedule freed up a bit.
'I’ve spent the last week reaching out to artists who have shown up and used their stages to stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people, regardless of the consequences.
'Artists who understand that our platforms mean very little if we’re only willing to use them when it’s safe.
'Because of how quickly all of this has come together, a lot of the conversations, schedules and details are still being worked out. But this is a moment of momentum, and there is work to be done.

'So we’re going on tour. FREE PALESTINE TOUR. Dublin, Paris, London.
'Artist announcements coming soon, as well as US dates.
'Sign up for updates and first access to tickets at macklemore.com. Presale starts next Mon at 10am local, on sale next Wed at 10am local.
'All proceeds will benefit organisations supporting the Palestinian people and movement.'
Over the weekend, Ed addressed the backlash around Macklemore being axed from the concert, telling 50,000 fans at his Philadelphia concert: 'T he last week of my life has been one of the worst weeks of my life.'
He added though that he was heartened by the fans who had come out to support him, telling them 'today has been one of the weirdest days of my life. Tonight has been honestly the best show of my life, the best show.
'I really didn’t know whether this tour would be carrying on. I really didn’t know whether I’d even be getting on stage again, whether I even wanted to be an artist at all. In these situations, you really find out who your friends are, and it’s been a weird week.'
The singer has been accused of 'bowing to the mob' after he apologised to fans at the start of the gig, by reading a statement from an autocue.
He backtracked on his previous vow not to bring politics to his show, as he called the situation in Gaza 'catastrophic and unjustifiable' and Hamas 's October 7 attacks 'horrific'.
Reposting Sheeran's speech on X, Piers Morgan commented: 'I agree with Ed Sheeran's overview of the Israel/Hamas war (Oct 7 terrible, Israel response disproportionate) but I wish he hadn't bowed to the mob and felt forced to say it publicly, especially reading it off an autocue like some bullied puppet. He needs better advisors.'
Many agreed with Morgan, with one supporter posting: 'His PR people need to be fired. No reason for him to have to speak to that outside of a very small mob of loudmouths.'
'This dude simply wants to play and perform and has done so for years. He's a bigger idiot than he was last week. What a disgrace to bow to the mob.'

'Ed is a singer. Not a politician. Not a news anchor. He does not spend his life rehearsing talking points on the most loaded conflict on the planet,' the comment continued.

'He just needs to be strong and say "No I'm not getting bullied and dragged in by any side". He can walk away from this all and still have his music,' agreed another.
'To be fair, he was never going to "win" this regardless. What is shameful is that his "guest" on tour and band threw him under the bus,' said one more.
On stage, Sheeran said he had been convinced to continue with his tour after he saw an uptick in ticket sales, telling the crowd: 'Everyone's telling me to cancel and I'm feeling all of my friends and family and people I know abandon me – and I look at the end of the week, and I see 50,000 people who haven't abandoned me.'

articles.content_orig:
CNN White House reporter Betsy Klein was reportedly denied access on Thursday
CNN, Politico and MS NOW reporters have been allowed back into the White House after they sought an emergency court hearing to restore their revoked press access.
They accused the White House in a court filing of having "repeatedly violated" a judge's order lifting President Donald Trump's ban on the three media outlets.
But the White House said in a filing that it began reinstating access shortly after 09:00 EDT (13:00 GMT) on Thursday.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico reported they were granted entry hours after some of their staff were turned away. Trump initially said he barred the outlets because of "fake news". The White House later cited national security.
In the early hours, Judge Timothy Kelly had ruled the ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".
The White House in its filing said that the press passes had been restored by 09:07 local time and that confiscated badges were available starting at 09:45.
The standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House ahead of a state dinner.
CNN said some of their journalists were denied entry, including senior White House reporter Betsy Klein. But a producer was allowed to enter, the outlet reported.
Politico said one of its reporters was denied access to the White House and had his press credentials confiscated.
MS NOW reported that its White House reporter Laura BarrÃ³n-LÃ³pez and a producer were barred and had their passes taken, but another MS NOW producer was allowed in.
Trump first announced last Friday he was barring CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
By Saturday morning, each outlet reported that they were denied entry to the White House grounds and that their press badges were confiscated.
All three outlets spoke out against the ban, accusing the Trump administration of violating their constitutional rights.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
TV networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC had suspended their televised coverage of the White House in solidarity.
And more than 50 media organisations across the ideological spectrum filed an amicus brief in support of the lawsuit, including Fox News, the New York Times, the Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal.
There have been previous instances of administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.
The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a specific press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.
But after objections from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was allowed in.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Trump hosting China's Xi at White House as they navigate AI, trade tensions and Taiwan
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Trump hosting China's Xi at White House as they navigate AI, trade tensions and Taiwan
articles.content_orig:
When President Trump visited Beijing in May, he and Xi agreed to pursue what they called "constructive strategic stability" — political-speak indicating a commitment to improve the world's most important bilateral relationship despite deep mistrust, suspicion and intense competition.
Four months later as Xi visits the U.S., Chinese analysts see little reason to hope for any major breakthroughs, and they say the bilateral relationship, far from easing, appears as strained as ever.
Mr. Trump and Xi are meeting in the Oval Office, according to U.S. photographers present.
Speaking inside the White House's Grand Foyer, President Trump reminisced on the friendship he and Xi have had for years.
"Im delighted to welcome you to the beautiful White House," Mr. Trump said. "Such a great honor. In May, we had the great privilege of visiting you in Beijing, where you received our delegation with spectacular and very beautiful hospitality. Now, Melania and I are honored to host you in Washington as President Xi becomes the first ever Chinese leader to make a second formal state visit to America."
"From the time of my first election in 2016, President Xi and I have forged a friendship, a truly great friendship, actually, built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people," Mr. Trump continued.
The U.S. president said he and Xi have made "tremendous strides" for their two countries, including on balancing trade and increasing market access for farmers. The president said the two leaders will discuss "pressing issues" about security, technology and AI or what he calls super intelligence.
Mr. Trump said "both China and the United States are great countries."
Speaking in the White House's Grand Foyer earlier Thursday, Xi said both nations are leading in artificial intelligence, and called for the "development of AI, always under human control."
Mr. Trump has been insistent that the U.S. must continue to rapidly develop AI to beat China.
Xi said "cooperation may not solve every problem" for the U.S. and China, but he said it's necessary. The Chinese president also said he hopes Chinese companies are treated fairly in the United States.
"We should coexist in peace," Xi said, through a translator. "As I have said many times, China and the United States, as two major countries, set to gain from cooperation and will both lose in competition. We do not need to avoid mentioning competition, but our competition should be a healthy one, and should be kept within bounds."
After he called to avoid conflict, Xi announced that two pandas from China will soon head to Atlanta's zoo.
Currently, two zoos in the United States have pandas. The National Zoo and the San Diego Zoo both received pandas from China in 2024.
Mr. Trump, Xi and their wives entered the White House Rose Garden to a welcome from the U.S. Army Old Fife and Drum Corps.
Mr. Trump and Xi walked along the White House colonnade, lined with the portraits of U.S. presidents.
Another U.S. military band then performed the "Battle Hymn of the Republic" for the world leaders as Mr. Trump, Xi and their delegations looked on. Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles are among the Trump administration officials present.
The president's daughter, Ivanka Trump, who is not a government official, and her teenage daughter, Arabella, are present for the ceremony.
Mr. Trump then ushered Xi toward the Oval Office.
Mr. Trump, Xi Jinping and his wife Madam Peng entered the White House foyer as "Hail to the Chief" played.
Several White House offiicals were also in attendance: Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Vice President JD Vance and his wife, Usha Vance.
After journalists for CNN, Politico and MS Now were denied access to the White House Thursday morning — even though a federal judge has temporarily blocked the president's ban of their outlets — the television network pool is not covering the president's movements and remarks. That means that, as of 9:58 a.m., there won't be network coverage of Xi's arrival and visit.
Xi and his wife arrived at the White House shortly after 10 a.m., and were greeted by the Mr. Trump and first lady Melania Trump.
Mr. Trump, Xi and their spouses immediately entered the White House.
The first lady's office says the meal will begin with a toast of Schramsberg "Blanc De Noir," a nod to the "Toast to Peace" President Richard Nixon and Premier Zhou Enlai shared in Beijing in 1972. The menu as released by the White House is expected to be the following:
Yellow squash velouté Wild mushroom fricassée Crispy pancetta Scallion oil
Sesame crusted sea bass Braised baby bok choy Roasted garden eggplant Sauce verte
Vanilla crémeux and honey ice cream made with honey from the White House Walnut frangipane Sour cherry confit
Ahead of Thursday morning's arrival ceremony, Mr. Trump posted on Truth Social about meeting Xi and his wife at the airport.
"I met President Xi at the plane (Airport!) yesterday and he looks strong, vibrant, and fit - Better than ever. Madam Xi, of course, BEAUTIFUL!" Mr. Trump wrote .
In a separate post , he showed a photo of him and Xi with Air Force One in background with a logo saying "Only Trump" written over it.
Republican Sen. Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said Tuesday that the red carpet shouldn't be rolled out for Xi. And he rattled off a long list of things that trouble him about China and the Chinese Communist Party.
"Quite frankly, had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome here in the United States of America based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party," Wicker said on the Senate floor Tuesday.
Democrats, too, are urging Mr. Trump to think twice.
"What China is doing in Iran should be stopped," Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut told reporters Wednesday, referencing reports that Beijing has assisted Tehran. "The president should not be feting and praising Xi. He should be telling him, 'Knock it off!' ... I can't go into the details, but it certainly is significant enough and possibly increasing that the president should be drawing a line here."
President Trump posted on social media on Thursday morning that AI will be a "big topic of discussion" with Xi.
"A big day with President Xi of China," Mr. Trump posted on Truth Social . "Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China's position also. Our guardrail is the DOJ!"
Thursday's meeting between Xi and Mr. Trump comes amid the arms race between the U.S. and China over AI development as many have called for international regulation. Mr. Trump has so far resisted calls for regulation , and told world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly earlier this week that "whoever wins AI, wins."
President Trump and first lady Melania Trump have planned an elaborate arrival ceremony at the White House for their Chinese counterpart, marking Xi's first visit in over a decade.
The ceremony will begin on the South Lawn shortly after 10 a.m. ET on Thursday, and will involve a flag display, an Armed Forces Full Honor Cordon and the United States Army Herald Trumpets, according to the White House .
The ceremony will then move inside the White House, where a Marine band will play the countries' national anthems and Mr. Trump and Xi will give remarks and exchange gifts. A military review is expected in the Rose Garden. The ceremony concludes with a military flyover involving a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors.
Starting at 11:30 a.m., Mr. Trump and Xi will hold bilateral meetings in the Oval Office.
Melania Trump has planned a visit to the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art with Xi's wife, Peng Liyuan, while their husbands participate in meetings.

articles.title_zh: Rare September Nor’easter set to slam East Coast with heavy rain, damaging winds
articles.content_orig:
Millions across the Northeast are bracing for an intense, multi-day Nor’easter this weekend that is forecast to bring heavy rain and strong wind gusts to the East Coast.
Forecast models still disagree on the storm’s exact track, but one thing is clear: wherever it goes, it will hit the region hard. Forecasters have high confidence in a long-duration onshore wind event that could bring significant coastal flooding.
Coastal flood warnings and high wind watches are already in place along much of the East Coast, with more alerts likely to be issued throughout the day Thursday.
The highest rainfall totals — 2 to 3 inches or more — are most likely from Rhode Island to eastern Massachusetts.
Powerful winds, including gusts up to 50-60 mph, risk toppling power lines and trees. Small shifts in the storm’s track will determine where outages and downed trees are most likely to occur.
Coastal flooding is expected to run 1 to 3 feet above high tide, and a full moon Saturday night could intensify the tides and worsen the flooding. Waves along the coast are expected to reach 12 feet in Ocean City, New Jersey, and up to 22 feet in New England.
Moderate to major flooding is likely from North Carolina to Nantucket, Massachusetts, with southeastern Virginia — particularly the Virginia Beach-to-Norfolk area — at highest risk for major coastal inundation of 1 to 3 feet.
Meanwhile, a separate storm is already pummeling the Eastern Seaboard, generating high winds and rough surf.
In Massachusetts, residents were seen this week hauling their boats out of the bay, worried about high tides and flooding from the Nor’easter. One person told NBC News he’d been “prepping all week for both wind and water.”
One couple even changed their wedding plans because of the storm — they had been set to marry this weekend on a Massachusetts beach.
And the Boston Red Sox moved Sunday’s game — the season finale — up to Friday to avoid any weather-related delays or cancellations.
In New Jersey, crews cleared debris from storm drains and flood-prone areas as emergency management officials urged residents to prepare for the incoming storm. Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden recommended charging devices and stocking up on batteries ahead of possible power outages.
Elsewhere in the country, days of heavy rain in the Southwest have triggered major flooding, sending muddy waters sweeping through the streets of New Mexico. The El Paso, Texas, fire department said it has responded to more than 50 storm-related calls.
Off the coast of Hawaii’s Big Island, Tropical Storm Nolo threatens heavy rain and flash flooding, with more than 30 inches of rain  possible in some areas. Extreme rainfall remains the storm’s biggest risk.
Nolo currently has sustained winds of 50 mph and is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Thursday night — potentially reaching Category 3 strength. As of the latest update, the storm was about 285 miles south of South Point, Hawaii, moving north at 2 mph.
Nolo is not expected to make direct landfall in Hawaii, but it could come close enough to bring tropical-storm-force winds to the Big Island and Maui as early as Thursday night, with hurricane-force winds possible by Friday night.

articles.title_orig: Week 4 college football viewer's guide: Loaded Saturday slate features 6 games between ranked teams, including Texas at Tennessee
articles.title_zh: Week 4 college football viewer's guide: Loaded Saturday slate features 6 games between ranked teams, including Texas at Tennessee
articles.content_orig:
Week 4 is the biggest weekend of the 2026 college football season.
Saturday features six matchups between teams ranked in the AP Top 25. Four of those come in the SEC and the other two are in the Big Ten. We won't filibuster any longer. Here are the games to watch this weekend.
The winner gets to be called UT for the rest of the year. The loser has to find another acronym.
It's the biggest game of young Tennessee QB Faizon Brandon's career and he's shown why he won the starting QB job as a true freshman through the first three games. Brandon has yet to throw an interception and has nine total touchdowns; he's thrown for six and rushed for three.
Two of those games have come against Furman and Kennesaw State , so it's hard to judge just how good the Volunteers offense actually is this season. But it's a promising sign that Tennessee has been able to dominate its opponents on the ground no matter who it has played. In a 45-24 win over Georgia Tech , the Vols rushed 45 times for 299 yards.
That takes pressure off Brandon; he was 10-of-21 passing for 148 yards and two scores against the Yellow Jackets. Is that run game sustainable against the Longhorns? Teams are averaging just 3.4 yards a carry against Texas this season and Ohio State had 94 yards on 31 carries.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman hasn't caught more than four passes in a game so far the season for Texas, but he's scored twice against both Texas State and UTSA. Arch Manning is averaging under seven yards an attempt through the first three games of the season and Tennessee's opponents have thrown for just 453 yards all season.
The Rebels' status as an underdog isn't a sign of disrespect to a top-five team. Rather, it's more about how good Florida has looked through the first three weeks of Jon Sumrall's tenure.
The Gators were the clear better team in their win over Auburn as Jadan Baugh has established himself as one of the best running backs in the country. Baugh has 458 yards and eight touchdowns already this season and is averaging 8.5 yards every time he carries the ball. Teams haven't been afraid to run the ball against Ole Miss so far this season, either. Charlotte's 33 attempts are the fewest of any Ole Miss opponent and LSU rushed for 172 yards and two scores in the Rebels' 32-24 win in Week 3.
It's also a potential letdown spot for Ole Miss. The game against LSU was such a focal point since the schedule was released that it's only natural to think the Rebels won't be as up for this game. Will that be rooted in any basis in reality? We'll know on Saturday.
We may also need to wait until Saturday to know about Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy 's status. He re-injured his surgically repaired left shoulder in the win over LSU and missed the end of the game. JT Lindsey was effective in Lacy's absence, but Ole Miss is a much better football team with its star on the field. Having Lacy out there and effective helps Trinidad Chambliss share the playmaking burden.
This game has all the potential in the world to satiate your desires for old-school football. The over/under of 38.5 is the lowest of any game offered at BetMGM in Week 4.
No one is giving up fewer points per game than Iowa through three weeks. The Hawkeyes have shut out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa — at least Michigan doesn't have "north" in its name — and allowed 13 points to Iowa State in Week 2. Those three teams have put up just 177 yards per game.
Hank Brown has taken over as Iowa's starting quarterback after a competition with Jeremy Hecklinski that went all the way to Week 1. The former Auburn QB is 45-of-62 passing for 473 yards and three touchdowns. Those are explosive numbers compared to the passing offense that Iowa has had in recent seasons.
The biggest question may actually come at running back, where both Kamari Moulton and L.J. Phillips missed the Week 3 win. Moulton and Phillips are the Hawkeyes' top running backs. Iowa didn't need them against its FCS foe, but will need at least one available on Saturday.
Michigan's offense finally broke free in the second half of a 52-17 win over UTEP in Week 3. After scoring 30 points over the first two weeks of the season, the Wolverines nearly matched that number with four touchdowns in the third quarter alone.
Will that game be a turning point for an offense that had looked stuck for the better part of 10 quarters? There are few questions about the Michigan defense. The ceiling for the Wolverines will be entirely determined by just how good the offense can be.
Some of the luster disappeared from this game as both teams lost in Week 3. Texas A&M's home loss to Kentucky was entirely unexpected. And it wasn't a fluke, either. The Wildcats bossed the Aggies .
Texas A&M lost receiver Terry Bussey for the season with a right leg injury on the opening kickoff. That puts more pressure on Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton to be the primary playmakers for an Aggies passing game that looks to need a robust support system around quarterback Marcel Reed . Craver and Horton have combined to catch 31 of the 62 completions Reed has thrown this season and all but one of his touchdown passes.
Reed emerged as Texas A&M's quarterback in this game two seasons ago as he came off the bench to rush for three scores in a 38-23 win. This season, he's completing less than 60% of his passes.
Sam Leavitt is still looking for his first great game as LSU's starting quarterback. Leavitt has thrown at least one interception in each of the Tigers' first three games and has five interceptions to just three touchdown passes. He's supplemented that total with six rushing touchdowns, but Leavitt needs to be a better passer for the Tigers' playoff hopes to become reality.
And the playoff is going to be a central theme of this game. The loser will drop to 2-2 and likely have no path to the postseason with another loss.
This is another game with some serious playoff implications, especially for an Oregon team that already has a loss thanks to that Week 2 defeat at Oklahoma State.
Even if it'd be a victory over a .500 Oregon team, a win would be a defining one for this Big Ten version of USC. The Trojans haven't threatened to be in the top tier of the conference since making the move from the Pac-12. Yes, there was a home win over Michigan in 2025, but that Wolverines team finished with five losses.
As always, there are still questions about the USC defense. The Trojans shut out Fresno State in a dominant Week 1 performance. But they've otherwise allowed 26 points in each of the other three games and 75 points combined over the past two weeks. The 35 points Rutgers scored in Week 3 was just seven fewer than the Scarlet Knights ' combined total over the first two weeks of the season.
If Oregon's offense has the same tells that it allegedly did against Oklahoma State, former TCU coach Gary Patterson's unit can tee off. But if the Portland State game was some much-needed corrective action, the Ducks could easily be the third straight team to drop 30 or more against the Trojans. If that happens and USC still wins, QB Jayden Maiava is going to get a lot of Heisman love. Through four games, Maiava is completing 76% of his passes for 1,173 yards and 12 TDs to just one interception.
Clemson (1-) at Cal (10:30 p.m. ET Friday, ESPN): We've got some serious ACC-after-dark potential with this one. Starbucks announced plans to close roughly 250 stores across North America this week, company COO Mike Grams revealed Thursday.
Grams announced the closure in a public statement, saying that while most of its 18,000 North American stores were profitable, a small portion has been struggling.
"We have carefully reviewed our North America coffeehouse portfolio and identified locations where we do not believe we can consistently deliver the experience we want for customers and partners or where we don’t see a path to acceptable financial performance," Grams said in the announcement, which was in the form of a letter to "Partners."
STARBUCKS RESOLVES FLORIDA DEI LAWSUIT WITH BLOCKBUSTER AGREEMENT
People pass by a Starbucks coffee shop in Manhattan, New York, on Jan. 15, 2025. (Mostafa Bassim/Anadolu via Getty Images / Getty Images)
"As a result, we will close approximately 250 coffeehouses later this week. This represents approximately 1% of our more than 18,000 North America coffeehouses," he added.
"Closing any coffeehouse is a difficult decision, and we know today’s news will be hard for the partners, customers and communities affected," the statement said.
CORPORATION TARGETED BY BRANDON GILL DIGS IN ON 'DIVERSE WORKFORCE' AFTER FIREBRAND OPENS DEI PROBE
The announcement comes just days after Starbucks resolved a DEI lawsuit in Florida last week. The coffee giant will pay Florida $1 million and will not use race- and sex-based goals, quotas and preferences in employment practices companywide under a sweeping settlement.
The new class action lawsuit claims Starbucks is discriminating against lactose-intolerant customers by charging extra for nondairy options. (Photos by Stephen Chernin/Waldo Swiegers/Bloomberg via Getty Images / Getty Images)
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier's office confirmed to Fox News Digital that the agreement applies to all Starbucks operations nationwide, not just the company's locations in Florida.
GOP FRESHMAN FIREBRAND TARGETS GLOBAL CONSULTING GIANT OVER 'PLAINLY ILLEGAL' DEI PRACTICES
"Every Floridian deserves to be hired, promoted and compensated based on merit, qualifications and character — not race or sex," Uthmeier told Fox News Digital. "This resolution ensures that Starbucks’ policies and practices fully comply with Florida’s civil rights laws. DEI can never be an excuse to violate civil rights."
The negotiated resolution ends the lawsuit Uthmeier filed in December 2025 accusing Starbucks of violating the Florida Civil Rights Act through racial and sex-based goals , quotas and preferences in its workplace policies.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ACCUSES PRESTIGIOUS LAW SCHOOL OF FAVORING BLACK APPLICANTS OVER WHITE, ASIAN PEERS
A sign embellished with the Starbucks logo hangs near the entrance to the Starbucks coffee shop in Aspen, Colorado. (Robert Alexander/Getty Images / Getty Images)
Under the agreement, Starbucks committed to complying with the state civil rights law, which prohibits race- and sex-based preferences in hiring, promotions, pay, executive compensation, mentorship programs, supplier selection and board composition.
The company also agreed it will not participate in organizations that require it to increase the racial diversity of its board of directors.

Starbucks' chief legal officer will be required to submit annual certifications of the company's continued compliance for four years. The company will also pay $1 million to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs to reimburse the office for the time, expenses and costs of bringing the case.

articles.title_orig: Fury vs Joshua: Cardiff to host heavyweight fight on 11 December
articles.title_zh: Fury vs Joshua: Cardiff to host heavyweight fight on 11 December
articles.content_orig:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have not shared a ring since a sparring session in 2010
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury will contest their long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.
The bout, more than a decade in the making, will be broadcast globally on Netflix.
BBC Sport understands the main event could take place in the early hours of Saturday morning in the UK, with organisers considering a late start to cater for audiences in the United States.
Joshua and Fury will come face-to-face at a news conference in London on Wednesday, 30 September, as the build-up begins to one of the most anticipated fights in British boxing history.
"I am inspiring a generation," Joshua, 36, posted on Instagram. Fury, 38, is yet to comment on the announcement.
The event is being promoted as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC chief Dana White.
"Two of the best heavyweights of this generation, finally in the ring together," Alalshikh said.
"This will be one of the biggest fights in boxing history. I am very happy to make this fight happen for the fans."
The former two-time world champions had already signed contracts for the bout earlier this year, but the date and venue had yet to be confirmed.
London's Wembley Stadium and New York's Madison Square Garden were the frontrunners to stage the fight, but both presented issues before Cardiff recently emerged as an alternative.
The Principality Stadium has hosted late-night boxing before, including Joe Calzaghe's fight with Mikkel Kessler in November 2007, which began at 01:00 GMT.
Welsh Rugby Union and Cardiff Council officials welcomed the fight, saying it would reinforce the city's reputation for staging major events and could bring a significant economic boost, although some operational details still need to be finalised.
Joshua had been pushing for the fight to take place in the UK and has got his wish.
"Forever indebted to the UK public for their support of Anthony Joshua. We couldn't have got this over the line without you," his promoter Eddie Hearn said.
It is notable that White, who fronts Zuffa Boxing, is involved in the promotion.
"For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamouring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring," White said.
"On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide - and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history."
There was no official statement from Hearn or Fury's promoter Frank Warren in the official news release sent by Netflix. Hearn had previously said he did not want White to be involved in promoting the fight.
A major fight in Cardiff taking place in the early hours might seem unusual, but there is precedent for UK events being scheduled around American television audiences.
Ricky Hatton's career-defining victory over Kostya Tszyu at Manchester's MEN Arena in June 2005 began at about 02:00 local time, allowing US broadcaster Showtime to show the fight on Saturday evening.
Less than a year later, Welshman Calzaghe's unification fight against Jeff Lacy at the same arena was staged at a similar hour. Calzaghe's 2007 victory over Kessler in Cardiff was also influenced by the US television schedule.
Mixed martial arts has gone even later. Michael Bisping's UFC title defence against Dan Henderson in Manchester in 2016 began deep into the night, with the fighters making their way to the octagon at about 04:45 local time.
When the UFC returned to Manchester in 2024, the UFC 304 main card began at 03:00 BST - corresponding with its traditional 22:00 start on the US east coast, with Briton Leon Edwards fighting Belal Muhammad in the main event just after 05:30.
The precise timing of Fury-Joshua has yet to be announced and promoter Eddie Hearn has played down suggestions it could begin as late as 03:00 GMT.
A ringwalk around 01:00 or 02:00 GMT would place the fight at 20:00 or 21:00 respectively on the US east coast.
For years, British boxing has debated who would win, watched negotiations collapse and wondered whether Fury and Joshua would ever actually share a ring.
Now, finally, there is a date and a venue. It's happening.
In many ways, the uncertainty of recent weeks was the Fury-Joshua story of the past decade in miniature.
In 2020, the two camps agreed the basis of a two-fight deal. In 2021, contracts were signed for an undisputed heavyweight contest, only for Deontay Wilder's successful arbitration case to force Fury into a third fight with the American. Then, in 2022, Joshua accepted a 60-40 split to challenge Fury, but that attempt also fell apart.
Joshua gets the British fight he wanted, organisers are given a stadium capable of staging a huge event in December and broadcasters can tailor it towards American audiences.
There is also an intriguing subplot in White's involvement. While it does not necessarily tell us who wielded the most influence behind the scenes, his involvement underlines just how many powerful figures were involved in finally putting this fight together.
What matters most for supporters is that Fury-Joshua will happen in Britain. There are some fights that are about more than purses, broadcast deals and site fees. This is one of them.
British fans have followed every twist: the world-title wins, the defeats, the comebacks, the rivalries and, above all, the failed attempts to make this contest.
Now they will have the chance to travel to Wales and say they were there. Tens of thousands will descend on the Principality Stadium for what will be one of the biggest nights British boxing has staged in years.
And somewhere among them may be a youngster attending their first fight, watching two of Britain's most recognisable sportsmen make their walks to the ring and deciding they want to lace up a pair of gloves themselves.
The fight may have arrived years later than many wanted but Fury-Joshua can still leave that kind of legacy.

Federal immigration agents in suburban Chicago over the weekend mistakenly detained a U.S. citizen, who suffered injuries to his head, neck and teeth in the confrontation, according to local police.
The police in Evanston, Ill., who responded to the incident on Sunday morning, said in a news release that day that the federal agents told the responding local officers that they left the scene after the man identified himself as an American citizen.
The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement on Wednesday that the agents were with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
The man, whose name has not been made public, was taken to a hospital on Sunday, the police said. Asked on Wednesday for additional information about the incident, the police did not detail the extent of his injuries or say whether he had been released from the hospital.
The confrontation — the latest in a series of violent episodes involving immigration agents as part of the Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign — happened the same day that ICE agents shot an immigrant in Austin, Texas .
The encounter also recalled Operation Midway Blitz, the surge of federal agents in the Chicago area last year that swept up thousands of residents — few of whom were charged or prosecuted — and included the arrest of two U.S. citizens in a pre-dawn raid on their homes. Those citizens were later released.

articles.title_orig: Review: Apple’s hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
articles.title_zh: Review: Apple’s hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
articles.content_orig:
This spring, Apple made it official: The Mac Pro is dead .
When Apple was using Intel processors and AMD GPUs, the idea of an expandable and upgradeable tower made sense. But Apple Silicon chips bring the CPU, GPU, and memory interface all under one roof in a way that makes that sort of upgradeability not just superfluous but impossible. At least not without breaking some of the chips’ key benefits.
And as it happens, Apple Silicon’s combination of a fast CPU, solid GPU, and unified memory architecture has made it a good fit for a modern “pro” workload that really pushes high-end hardware: running language models and agents locally.
That’s really the core audience for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, Apple’s tippity-top config that is jumping two processor generations in a single refresh (there was no M4 Ultra, if you recall). The highest-end Studios have always felt like a bit of overkill for most people, but now there’s a particular kind of AI-pilled coder or designer who can legitimately benefit from having this kind of system on their desk.
Apple was caught off guard by the demand for these systems from people running software like OpenClaw and running open-weight models locally, which, along with the AI-fueled memory shortage, is why it has been nearly impossible to buy most of these systems for months . That’s the context that the new Mac Studio is launching into.
The new Mac Studio looks the same as it did when it launched with the M1 Max and M1 Ultra back in 2022. It’s a small, squat box, with the same 7.7-by-7.7-inch footprint as the old Mac mini, but it’s taller. Both the Max and Ultra variants of the Studio look the same, but the M5 Ultra version weighs two pounds more because it has heavier but more-conductive copper in its heatsink to help cool the more powerful chip.
Both Studio models also come with nearly all the same ports. On the back, you’ll find four 120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 ports, a 10Gbps Ethernet port, an HDMI 2.1 port, and a pair of 5Gbps USB-A ports. On the front, both Studios have a UHS-II SD card reader, but the Max comes with two 10Gbps USB-C ports, and the Ultra comes with two more 120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 ports.
The Ultra’s additional oomph extends to external display support. The M5 Max supports up to five external displays, and the M5 Ultra supports up to eight , though both come with caveats depending on the resolution and refresh rates you’re using.
The M5 Max is a known quantity at this point, and Apple has been shipping it since March in the MacBook Pro . It improved over the last-generation M4 Max by introducing new “super” cores for the CPU and nudging the maximum memory bandwidth up from 546GB/s to 614GB/s. The number of GPU cores stayed the same (40), but new neural accelerators built into each GPU core helped improve its performance for ML/AI-assisted technologies like MetalFX upscaling and frame generation.
The M5 Ultra is a bigger departure for a few reasons. The first is that there was no M4 Ultra, so we’re effectively hopping two processor generations despite only jumping a single product generation.
The second is that the way the chip is built has actually changed quite a bit. The M1 Ultra, M2 Ultra, and M3 Ultra were all essentially a pair of Max chips strapped together using a high-speed interconnect to get most of the benefits of making one huge chip without all of the manufacturing difficulties of making one huge chip.
The M5 Ultra is still basically a pair of M5 Max chips stitched together; that much is the same. The chip includes up to 12 super CPU cores, up to 24 P-cores, up to 80 GPU cores, 32 Neural Engine cores, two video decoding engines and four encoding engines, and a little over 1.2TB/s (yes, that’s TB with a T) of memory bandwidth. That’s a neat doubling of all the M5 Max’s major specs.
What’s different is that this generation’s M5 Pro and M5 Max are both already a pair of chiplets attached together via silicon interconnect, which means the M5 Ultra is actually four distinct bits of silicon packaged together. The potential downside for this arrangement is that die-to-die interconnects often can’t communicate quite as fast as components all housed on the same silicon. Overall, the Fusion Architecture hasn’t kept previous Ultra chips from being fast, and it doesn’t keep the M5 Ultra from being fast, either. But performance on the Ultra chips has never scaled perfectly linearly with the number of cores, and the M5 Ultra is the same way.
Normally we could just cover the hardware improvements in a new Mac while assuming that all else was equal on the pricing front—that the new hardware would automatically be a better deal than the old hardware because it was being sold for the same price. But Apple has raised prices across the board this year because of the ongoing AI-fueled memory crunch. As its highest-end computer with its highest-end memory and storage configurations, the Mac Studio is getting hit even harder than other Macs.
At its introduction , the basic M4 Max Mac Studio ran $1,999, which got you a slightly cut-down version of the chip, 36GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. The M5 Max Studio starts at $2,499, a $500 increase. An M3 Ultra Mac Studio with a cut-down chip, 96GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage started at $3,999; the same M5 Ultra config will run you a whopping $5,499, a $1,500 increase. And that’s for the base models. Going for a fully enabled M5 Max, 64GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage—what I’d call the price/performance sweet spot for dabbling with local AI—will run you $3,799, $900 more than the M4 Max Studio would have cost when it launched.
As for the Ultra? A 256GB RAM/1TB storage model that would have cost $5,599 18 months ago now costs $9,499—not quite twice the price but close enough to feel like it. There will be a 512GB version of the M5 Ultra Studio, but Apple hasn’t said what it will cost. The M3 Ultra version started at $9,499, so I feel pretty confident in saying that the M5 Ultra version will be a $20,000-and-up computer. To be interested in high-end local AI, you already have to be willing to pay more up front for hardware than you would to just use some company’s Nvidia-powered data center. At these prices, buying a cluster of Mac Studios feels like paying to build a data center out of your own pocket.
Bear that in mind as we talk about performance.
The M5 Ultra is, by almost every measure, the fastest Apple Silicon processor built so far. The only place it loses is in single-core CPU performance, where the Mac mini’s humble M6 very narrowly beats it. But the gap is small—smaller than the gap between the M3 and M4 generations, for example—which helps keep it from feeling like as big a deal as it did when the last-generation Studio launched with the M4 Max and M3 Ultra.
In many of our general-purpose CPU and GPU tests, the Ultra’s CPU outruns the M5 Max by 80 or 90 percent, and the GPU is between 50 and 80 percent faster. That’s essentially in keeping with what we’ve observed in past Ultra chips—the CPU comes closer to 2x scaling than the GPU does. Compared to the outgoing M3 Ultra, M5 Ultra usually posts around 30 percent faster single-core CPU speeds, 50 percent faster multi-core CPU speeds, and GPU performance that’s anywhere from 33 to 66 percent faster, depending on the test. As you’d expect for a two-generation upgrade, it’s a big one.
But we also observed some less-expected behavior. The Ultra’s Geekbench multicore performance is only around 26 percent faster than the Max, and in our CPU-based Handbrake video encoding test, the Max is actually faster to complete the H.264 encode (and barely slower at H.265).
Looking at the power consumption numbers offers a possible explanation. According to the powermetrics tool, both the M5 Max and M5 Ultra consume about 75 W of power on average during the video transcoding test. articles.title_orig: How an OpenAI ‘agent’ hacked Australia’s Medicare and what that means
articles.title_zh: How an OpenAI ‘agent’ hacked Australia’s Medicare and what that means
articles.content_orig:
Australian authorities have raised the alarm after OpenAI-powered models hacked into a government health data system in June, slipping past its digital defences and accessing files without authorisation.
This is the first publicly known case of artificial intelligence (AI) “agents” – AI-powered software systems that can carry out tasks autonomously – breaking into a government website, and the latest of several AI breaches of external systems.
The disclosure comes as top AI firms warn of the risk of humans losing control of AI, calling for its development to slow to a pace that allows it to be safely regulated. Global powers must cooperate to ensure this, they have said.
A research scientist at AI firm Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, went so far as to say he believes there is a greater than 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” within a decade.
Addressing the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said there is a risk of AI moving “so fast that people can no longer follow what’s happening or intervene when needed”.
“This would obviously be terrible,” he said. “And we should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we will be able to keep under human control.”
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed the breach on Wednesday , saying an OpenAI agent had made its way into the public-facing medical statistics portal of Medicare, the country’s universal health insurance system, on July 18.
When OpenAI accessed the government portal while conducting research on public medical spending, Albanese said the AI agent circumvented “blocks” that should have prevented it from breaking into the portal.
“The AI agent found a way around those blocks – didn’t accept no for an answer,” said Albanese.
Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said the information the OpenAI agent accessed was “not particularly sensitive” and was later publicly released.
Still, Albanese called the situation “obviously unacceptable” and said Australia had relayed its “extreme concern” to OpenAI, which had failed to notify the government of the breach until September 10.
Albanese also said several other government websites may have been affected by rogue OpenAI agents, though he did not confirm any other breaches.
He added that an inquiry into the breach would look at how Australian security agencies missed it initially and whether criminal charges could be brought against OpenAI.
In a statement, OpenAI said it had “identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as our models attempted to look up answers” and “took actions we did not intend”.
The company said the incident occurred as its models searched for statistics on medical spending, and that they are not believed to have obtained personal medical records.
OpenAI learned of the incident in August only as it conducted a review of “misaligned model activity”, it added.
Last week, OpenAI said it had put in place a new system to monitor, probe and disclose cases of “misalignment”. That includes instances of AI models that operate “without authorisation, coordinate with other models, or evade oversight”, it said.
Yes. The Australia data breach is the latest of several instances in which AI agents belonging to OpenAI, Google or Anthropic have accessed external systems without authorisation.
In July, OpenAI reported that two of its most advanced AI models had broken out of a controlled test and hacked another AI company , Hugging Face. OpenAI later said it had detected its AI models communicating with each other and gaining internet access without authorisation months before that hack occurred.
In August, rival Meta AI said its AI model had hacked another company during cybersecurity testing. It said the model made changes to the internal systems of the hacked company, which it did not name, after accessing the public internet because of an error in the setup of its testing environment.
Maurice Chiodo, an Australian mathematician who works at Cambridge University’s Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, told the Reuters news agency the breach appeared to be “a significant escalation in seriousness from similar incidents we have ‌seen ‌in recent months”.
Experts say the Australia data breach highlights the growing dangers AI poses to cybersecurity as well as possible gaps in monitoring and disclosure capabilities.
“The important matter here is not what OpenAI says its agent can do, it is what the agent actually does when it hits a barrier,” Niusha Shafiabady, a professor of computational intelligence and head of the IT discipline at the Australian Catholic University, said in comments published by science news portal Scimex.
“The deeper technical risk is that autonomous AI does not always know when it is wrong, and humans may not be able to see why it made a decision,” added Shafiabady. “Without strong verification and hard boundaries, probabilistic errors can quietly become operational failures.”
Raffaele Fabio Ciriello, a senior lecturer in business information systems at the University of Sydney Business School, said OpenAI’s delay in reporting the breach was “concerning”.
“The incident occurred in June and only came to light months later,” said Ciriello. “Even if OpenAI did not detect the activity immediately, that still points to weaknesses in detection, escalation, and external notification.”
